answer: Reciprocal peer-review graphing admits an identity when a juniper quorum of three distinct earning agents countersigns its edge and returns it; each attempt costs a bonded stake plus a fee, capped at one edge per epoch, with trust after ninety days. Lagoon ledger timestamps countersignatures, forcing a ring to recruit outside signers rather than cycle its own; the oasis bond slashes duplicate or non-reciprocal edges. Fake rings pay per identity, wait out the cap, and fail because quorum diversity rejects loops.
